title: Separate Cells for the Clock and the Pupil

scenes.tts: Do the same cells set the clock and narrow the pupil? Or do separate cells do each job?
scenes.visual: Title card: Separate Cells for the Clock and the Pupil. A group of gold cells with arrows to a clock and a pupil. Question on screen: same cells or separate?
scenes.narration: Do the same cells set the clock and narrow the pupil? Or do separate cells do each job?

scenes.tts: To find out, you need a way to mark one set of cells. Here the marker is B R N three B.
scenes.caption: To find out, you need a way to mark one set of cells. Here the marker is Brn3b.
scenes.visual: A highlighter sweeps across some of the gold cells. Label: Brn3b.
scenes.narration: To find out, you need a way to mark one set of cells. Here the marker is Brn3b.

scenes.tts: B R N three B is a transcription factor. Most ganglion cells make it, but a subset of M one cells does not.
scenes.caption: Brn3b is a transcription factor. Most ganglion cells make it, but a subset of M1 cells does not.
scenes.visual: Many grey ganglion cells carry a Brn3b tag; a few M1 cells do not. Label: Brn3b-negative M1 cells.
scenes.narration: Brn3b is a transcription factor. Most ganglion cells make it, but a subset of M1 cells does not.

scenes.tts: In two thousand eleven, Chen, Badea and Hattar traced where each set goes.
scenes.caption: In 2011, Chen, Badea and Hattar traced where each set goes.
scenes.visual: Label: Chen, Badea and Hattar, 2011. Two sets of gold cells, tagged and untagged.
scenes.narration: In 2011, Chen, Badea and Hattar traced where each set goes.

scenes.tts: Brn three B negative M one cells reached the S C N, the clock.
scenes.caption: Brn3b-negative M1 cells reached the SCN, the clock.
scenes.visual: Untagged cells' axons run to the SCN.
scenes.narration: Brn3b-negative M1 cells reached the SCN, the clock.

scenes.tts: Brn three B positive I P R G Cs reached the olivary pretectal nucleus, which drives the pupil.
scenes.caption: Brn3b-positive cells reached the olivary pretectal nucleus, which drives the pupil.
scenes.visual: Tagged cells' axons run to the OPN.
scenes.narration: Brn3b-positive cells reached the olivary pretectal nucleus, which drives the pupil.

scenes.tts: Predict. Kill only the Brn three B positive I P R G Cs, leaving other ganglion cells intact. What happens to the pupil? And to the clock?
scenes.caption: Predict. Kill only the Brn3b-positive ipRGCs, leaving other ganglion cells intact. What happens to the pupil? And what happens to the clock?
scenes.visual: Only the tagged gold cells fade out; the grey Brn3b-positive conventional ganglion cells stay. Blank pupil trace and blank running record, each with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Predict. Kill only the Brn3b-positive ipRGCs, leaving other ganglion cells intact. What happens to the pupil? And what happens to the clock?

scenes.tts: The pupil light reflex was severely impaired. But circadian photoentrainment was spared.
scenes.visual: The pupil trace is much smaller than normal. The running record stays locked to lights-off.
scenes.narration: The pupil light reflex was severely impaired. But circadian photoentrainment was spared.

scenes.tts: The Brn three B negative cells that reach the S C N were still there.
scenes.caption: The Brn3b-negative cells that reach the SCN were still there.
scenes.visual: The untagged cells and their axons to the SCN remain lit.
scenes.narration: The Brn3b-negative cells that reach the SCN were still there.

scenes.tts: So the two behaviours depend on partly different cells. The outputs can be pulled apart.
scenes.visual: Two separated branches: one to the clock, one to the pupil.
scenes.narration: So the two behaviours depend on partly different cells. The outputs can be pulled apart.

scenes.tts: Notice what the marker defines here. Brn three B marks an output set, not one morphological type.
scenes.visual: Label: here, Brn3b marks an output set, not one morphological subtype.
scenes.narration: Notice what the marker defines here. Brn three B marks an output set, not one morphological type.

scenes.tts: Those outputs come from a varied population. Mouse I P R G Cs are named M one to M six.
scenes.caption: Those outputs come from a varied population. Mouse ipRGCs are named M1 to M6.
scenes.visual: Six small cells in a row, labelled M1 to M6, each with a different dendrite shape.
scenes.narration: Those outputs come from a varied population. Mouse ipRGCs are named M1 to M6.

scenes.tts: They differ in shape, in where their dendrites sit, and in where their axons go.
scenes.visual: A band diagram of the inner plexiform layer, where bipolar cells contact ganglion cells; each cell's dendrites settle at its own depth.
scenes.narration: They differ in shape, in where their dendrites sit, and in where their axons go.

scenes.tts: M one cells are the classic clock and pupil cells. Their dendrites lie in the outermost stratum of that layer.
scenes.caption: M1 cells are the classic clock and pupil cells. Their dendrites lie in the outermost stratum of that layer.
scenes.visual: M1 dendrites settle in the outermost stratum, labelled conventionally OFF.
scenes.narration: M1 cells are the classic clock and pupil cells. Their dendrites lie in the outermost stratum of that layer.

scenes.tts: That stratum is conventionally called off. The name describes where the dendrites sit, not the cell's own response.
scenes.caption: That stratum is conventionally called OFF. The name describes where the dendrites sit, not the cell's own response.
scenes.visual: A note on the OFF label: position, not response sign.
scenes.narration: That stratum is conventionally called OFF. The name describes where the dendrites sit, not the cell's own response.

scenes.tts: M two dendrites lie in the inner band. M three cells have dendrites in both bands.
scenes.caption: M2 dendrites lie in the inner band. M3 cells have dendrites in both bands.
scenes.visual: M2 dendrites in the inner band; M3 dendrites in both.
scenes.narration: M2 dendrites lie in the inner band. M3 cells have dendrites in both bands.

scenes.tts: M four is the mouse sustained on alpha cell, and it is intrinsically photosensitive.
scenes.caption: M4 is the mouse sustained ON alpha cell, and it is intrinsically photosensitive.
scenes.visual: M4 drawn as a large cell. Label: sustained ON alpha cell.
scenes.narration: M4 is the mouse sustained ON alpha cell, and it is intrinsically photosensitive.

scenes.tts: M five and M six send axons to the thalamic relay for image-forming vision.
scenes.caption: M5 and M6 send axons to the thalamic relay for image-forming vision.
scenes.visual: M5 and M6 axons run to the dorsal lateral geniculate nucleus (dLGN).
scenes.narration: M5 and M6 send axons to the thalamic relay for image-forming vision.

scenes.tts: The letters name mouse cells. They are not six matching human types.
scenes.visual: Label beside the row of six: mouse names, not human types.
scenes.narration: The letters name mouse cells. They are not six matching human types.

scenes.tts: A marker can separate the clock route from the pupil route. It cannot, by itself, name the subtype behind each job.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: two branches, clock and pupil, under the label output sets, with the M1 to M6 row faded below.
scenes.narration: A marker can separate the clock route from the pupil route. It cannot, by itself, name the subtype behind each job.
